newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BOE says banks should stress test for EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: BOE says banks should stress test for EMU delay.

text.p: Banks should use sophisticated risk models to test their exposure to potential market upsets like a delay of the European single currency, Bank of England deputy governor Howard Davies said on Friday.

Davies said a delay of the single currency or a financial crisis in Japan were two examples of scenarios that banks should review with value-at-risk (VaR) models that check the impact on portfolios of various scenarios.

"The next step, which is already being taken in some cases, is for banks to develop models of market risk which allow them to calculate regulatory capital charges and to stress test their portfolios," Davies told a market risk seminar at the World Economic Forum here.

The Basle Committee on Banking Supervision, which groups banking supervisors from the Group of 10 (G10) industrial nations, will permit banks from end-1997 to use their own risk management models to calculate capital charges.
However, banks will only be allowed to use their own VaR models if they fulfill various qualitative criteria, including rigorous stress testing.

"Today, for example, banks should be asking themselves how they would be affected by a financial crisis in Japan or by a decision not to proceed with Economic and Monetary Union on the current timetable," he added.
Davies said these two events were not probable but were within the realm of possibilty and should therefore be encompassed in stress testing of portfolios.

European bankers have noted that many European bonds have converged in apparent market expectation that a single currency, or Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), will be launched in 1999 as planned by the European Union.
